In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UHE neutrino detection performances of a Mediterranean km 3 Neutrin Telescope are not affected by the site choice.

the UHE ντ detection capabilities of a km 2 Neutrino Telescope in the Mediterranean sea are not strongly dependent upon the site, provided that the water depth is sufficiently large to allow the full reconstruction of the ν τ events.
the UHE ντ detection performances of a KM3 Neutrino telescope are not significantly affected by the underwater surface profile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the limit of no detection efficiency and resolution, a km 3 telescope sitting at the ANTARES site is able to detect about the 10% of the ν τ fluxes expected in the atmosphere, while the same telescope sitting at the NEMO and the NESTOR sites would detect the 30% and the 50% respectively.
, for the three sites, the total yearly expected τ number in the km 3 detector volume is in the range 0.5-1.5.

, in the case of a neutrino telescope sitting in the Mediterranean sea and with a fiducial volume of 1 km 3, the yearly expected τ number is of the order of 10 4, 5 × 10 5 and 3 × 10 6 for NEMO, NESTOR and ANTARES, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the τ production rate is not affected by the surface profile, but the τ detection efficiency is.
the τ detection rate is not strongly affected by the site location, as it is mainly driven by the τ decay length.

the τ detection performances of km 3 telescopes sitting at different sites of the Mediterranean sea can vary of a factor of about 3, with the largest values being found for the ANTARES site, and the smallest values for the NESTOR site.
